sections.title: Authority and scope
sections.content: The self-hosted trust-recovery plan is governed by repository rules, lifecycle and Knowledge ADRs, Skill contracts, the lifecycle contract, and consumer policy. Lifecycle ownership remains separated: Maintainer authorizes implementation, Quick Dev owns implementation completion, and Acceptance owns acceptance passage. The plan does not authorize Knowledge publication, automatic Bootstrap startup, runtime/release actions, or historical-plan mutation. All supplied artifacts are non-authorizing.

sections.title: Repair findings
sections.content: Repair round 1 is limited to terminal argument/predicate compatibility, final receipt bindings, requirement and acceptance traceability, self-hosted authority declarations, protection of the immutable 2026-08-17 plan, and a clean RED baseline. Pre-existing shared workflow changes are outside slice write sets and require separate ownership or explicit disposition before plan-ready. Repair closure remains absent pending validation and maintainer authority prerequisites.

sections.title: Implementation slices
sections.content: R0 establishes a binding-derived persisted Acceptance evidence root and rejects request-local assertions or incomplete receipt bindings. R1 makes successor creation reentrant through reserved identity and byte-identical lineage, failing closed on conflicts. R2 preserves authorization across verified same-selection Knowledge refreshes while requiring reauthorization for selection, authority, scope, policy, contract, command, test, or protected-source drift. R3 verifies legacy prior-RED evidence only when selector, test bytes, execution fingerprint, and expected failures match. R4 performs read-only replay of 2026-08-17 evidence and publishes only new current bindings after R0-R3.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
sections.content: The command registry defines slice GREEN tests, per-slice terminal checks, full Quick Dev and Acceptance suites, and a terminal-full command. Each command uses structured executable/argv/cwd data with shell disabled. Slice dependencies are R0; R1 after R0; R2 and R3 after R1; R4 after R0-R3. Recovery rules resume only binding-derived persisted state, reuse identical successor reservations, replay frozen verified LKG selections, reject drift, and preserve historical evidence.

sections.title: Terminal contract
sections.content: The terminal validator computes a candidate binding from HEAD, tracked diff, and relevant untracked files; validates plan state, maintainer authorization, Knowledge context/freeze, Skill-input receipt, registered commands, and full-run slice receipts; and emits non-authorizing terminal results. Full completion additionally requires hashes for the implementation contract, command registry, authority manifest, Knowledge context and freeze, and a ready target-matching Skill-input receipt. Knowledge failures beyond ordinary catalog staleness require review; stale catalogs require a successor refresh. Terminal predicates are slice-ready for slices and implementation-complete for the full run.

sections.title: Acceptance invariants
sections.content: Persisted evidence and receipts must bind the current candidate, contracts, registries, Knowledge and Skill-input identities, events, and complete successor chains. Same-selection source refresh may continue only from verified published or LKG state without publishing new Knowledge authority. Missing sources, invalid ancestry or manifests, tampering, semantic selection drift, or authority-bearing source drift remain blockers. Historical authorization, terminal results, resume state, reports, and evidence under the 2026-08-17 plan remain immutable.
